stories.headline: Ousted South Korean President Yoon given prison term for drone flights over Pyongyang
stories.summary: South Korea's ousted President Yoon Suk Yeol and his former defense minister have been sentenced to 30 years in prison. The sentence was handed down in a case alleging Yoon ordered drone flights over Pyongyang in 2024. The flights were reportedly intended to heighten tensions with North Korea and justify declaring martial law in South Korea. The sentencing occurred on Friday, with both Yoon and his former defense minister receiving the same 30-year prison term. The case centers on allegations that Yoon's actions were aimed at escalating tensions with North Korea to justify domestic measures. The sentencing marks a significant development in the case against the ousted president and his former defense minister. Yoon's presidency was marked by controversy, and this sentencing is the latest in a series of events surrounding his ousting.

stories.headline: New migration rules are in force, but how will they work?
stories.summary: New EU migration rules are in effect, with Ireland opting in and required to comply. Meanwhile, in the US, a federal memo may force hundreds of thousands of visa holders to leave the country to apply for permanent residency. Recent updates to US immigration law include the OBBBA law, which increases detention and border wall budgets, and changes to USCIS marriage green card forms. Additionally, there have been TPS revocations for Hondurans and Nicaraguans, prolonged green card processing delays, and an increase in H-2B visas for temporary workers. The changes also include updated regulations, such as the OBBBA law, which may impact immigration processes. Affected immigrants are advised to seek immediate legal consultation to navigate the new regulations and landscape. Immigration laws and policies continue to evolve, with significant updates in 2026 affecting various aspects of immigration.

stories.headline: Has Donald Trump ruled out a strike on Iran's Kharg Island?
stories.summary: Donald Trump has cancelled planned strikes on Iran's Kharg Island, stating that "final points have been approved by all parties involved". This comes after Trump claimed that US strikes had "totally demolished" much of the island's oil export hub, although Iran has not confirmed this. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei reiterated that Tehran remains firm on its "red lines". Trump's latest statement suggests a potential de-escalation, with the possibility of a strike on Kharg Island now "off the table". The island has been a key target due to its importance in Iran's oil exports, and was considered for a strike after Iran's attack in October 2024. The situation remains unclear, with no official response from Iran or other countries mentioned by Trump. The cancellation of strikes may indicate a shift in the US approach to the situation.

stories.headline: Kenya: Government Allocates Sh177.2 Billion to Health Sector in Push for Universal Health Coverage
stories.summary: The Kenyan government has allocated Sh177.2 billion to the health sector in the 2026/27 budget. This significant investment aims to advance Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and strengthen essential services. Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi announced the allocation, which will be distributed across various healthcare initiatives. A substantial portion of the funds will go towards primary care, cancer centers, and referral hospitals. Additionally, medical interns will receive support. The allocation is part of the government's efforts to prioritize healthcare and improve access to quality medical services for all citizens. The funds will also be used to support community health promoters and other healthcare programs, marking a major boost to Kenya's health sector.

stories.headline: Ubisoft reportedly shuts down studios, puts nearly 380 jobs at risk Fresh reports suggest Ubisoft is closing studios in Canada and Serbia while cutting roles in Spain and the United States, extending a restructuring programme th
stories.summary: Ubisoft is reportedly shutting down its studios in Winnipeg, Canada, and Belgrade, Serbia, as part of a restructuring plan. The company will also restructure its Barcelona, Spain, office to focus solely on Rainbow Six projects. Approximately 380 jobs are at risk across the United States, Canada, Spain, and Serbia. The restructuring plan includes layoffs, buyouts, and operational changes, extending a program that has already led to job losses and downsizing. Ubisoft's global headcount will be further reduced, following repeated job losses and declining profits. The company's studio in Barcelona will prioritize Rainbow Six, while role reductions will occur within the Global Publishing team across the company. The changes aim to address slowed blockbuster game output and financial challenges faced by the gaming giant.

stories.headline: Microsoft just broke some custom folder icons, and it's deliberate Fortunately, there's an easy fix.
stories.summary: Microsoft has intentionally broken custom folder icons in a recent update. Fortunately, users can easily fix the issue. A possible solution is to use third-party apps like FolderIco, which allows users to change folder icons and colors in seconds. This app supports various formats, including JPG, PNG, and ICO, and enables customization of desktop, taskbar, and shortcut icons. Users can also find new custom icons for Windows through various online resources. Additionally, issues with Outlook Favorites and Windows 11 folder thumbnails can be resolved through simple troubleshooting steps, with guides available online, such as the 15 ways to fix folder thumbnail issues on lifewire.com. These fixes can help users restore their custom folder icons and maintain a personalized and organized workspace.

stories.headline: We went hands-on at the Xbox Games Showcase 2026 in LA. From the new Spyro to Call of Duty, check out our breakdown of every major reveal.
stories.summary: The Xbox Games Showcase 2026 took place in LA, featuring major reveals including a new Spyro game, Spyro: A Realm Beyond, showcased in a cinematic trailer. Other announcements included the return of exclusives, anniversary hardware, and games from Xbox. A total of 5 major announcements were made during the event. The showcase lasted 1.5 hours, with an additional 30 minutes dedicated to the new Gears game. Call of Duty was also highlighted during the event. The showcase provided a comprehensive look at Xbox's upcoming games and hardware, giving fans a glimpse into what's to come. The event concluded 5 days ago, with coverage and breakdowns of the announcements still emerging.

stories.headline: Hisense RGB-themed pop-up event lights up the new landmark of FIFA World Cup 2026™ /PRNewswire/ -- As an Official Sponsor of the FIFA World Cup 2026TM, Hisense launched its RGB-themed pop-up activation on June 9 at Hudson Yards in New York....
stories.summary: Hisense, an Official Sponsor of the FIFA World Cup 2026, launched an RGB-themed pop-up activation on June 9 at Hudson Yards in New York. The event featured FIFA official resources and a brand collaboration, showcasing the company's commitment to global sports partnerships. As the Origin of RGB MiniLED, Hisense continues to lead innovation in this field. The pop-up activation is part of the company's efforts to connect with audiences worldwide through sports. The event highlights Hisense's role as a major sponsor of the FIFA World Cup 2026, demonstrating its dedication to engaging with fans and promoting its brand on a global stage. The activation at Hudson Yards in New York serves as a landmark for the upcoming FIFA World Cup 2026.

stories.headline: One club, seven Socceroos: Melbourne team’s $1.2 million World Cup windfall A-League club Melbourne City has three current players in the Australian Socceroos squad for the FIFA World Cup in 2026 and four past players including Jordan B
stories.summary: Melbourne City is set to receive a $1.2 million windfall due to seven players with ties to the club being part of the Australian Socceroos squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Three current players and four past players, including Jordan, have connections to the A-League club. The Socceroos have a 26-player squad for the tournament, with a quarter of the players linked to Melbourne City. The team is led by a experienced coach and includes players like Nishan Velupillay, who has been selected to play for Australia after strong form in the A-League. The 2026 World Cup marks a significant milestone, with the Oceania Football Confederation granted one guaranteed slot and a possible second slot via inter-confederation play-offs. The tournament is co-hosted by Canada, Mexico, and the US, featuring 48 teams.

stories.headline: Boks already planning beyond Brown Despite confirming plans for life after Tony Brown, Rassie Erasmus says the Springboks still have plenty to learn from the attack guru.
stories.summary: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has confirmed that attack coach Tony Brown will remain with the team until the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia. After the tournament, Brown will join the All Blacks as an assistant coach under Dave Rennie. Despite knowing Brown's departure is imminent, Erasmus believes the team still has a lot to learn from him. Brown's contract with the Springboks will expire after the 2027 World Cup, at which point he will return to New Zealand to take up his new role. Erasmus has dismissed speculation about Brown's potential early departure, reaffirming that he will see out his contract with the Springboks. The team is already planning for life after Brown, but Erasmus is focused on maximizing the remaining time with the experienced attack coach.

stories.headline: World Cup 2026: Jude Bellingham highlights importance of feeling loved playing for England England midfielder Jude Bellingham stresses the importance of needing to 'feel loved' as he looks to help the Three Lions enjoy World Cup success this summer.
stories.summary: England midfielder Jude Bellingham has emphasized the importance of feeling loved and valued as he prepares for the World Cup. Bellingham, who scored once for England at Euro 2024, is not guaranteed a starting place in the team this summer. He has missed much of 2026 due to a hamstring injury, making it challenging to assess his current form. Despite this, Bellingham has earned a spot in England's squad for the World Cup. England's boss, Thomas Tuchel, has sent a brutal message to Bellingham on the eve of the tournament, indicating that his role is not secure. Bellingham will aim to help the Three Lions achieve success in the World Cup, and his performance will be closely watched. His ability to offer balance in the middle of the park will be crucial to England's campaign.

stories.headline: New documentary charts Coventry City's rollercoaster return to the Premier League BBC CWR's Richard Williams charts the Sky Blues' 25-year journey back to the top flight.
stories.summary: A new documentary, "Back Where We Belong: 25 years of Sky Blue Heartache and Hope," charts Coventry City's 25-year journey back to the Premier League. The six-episode series, produced by BBC CWR's Chloee French and reporter Richard Williams, a lifelong Sky Blues fan, explores the team's rollercoaster return to the top flight. Williams spent over three months working on the project. The documentary is available to listen to, offering a detailed look at the team's highs and lows over the past quarter century. BBC CWR's coverage of Coventry City also includes discussions with the Sky Blues Fancast panel, analyzing key talking points and developments surrounding the team. The documentary provides an in-depth examination of the team's journey back to the Premier League.

stories.headline: US admits attack on tanker that killed three Indian seafarers
stories.summary: The US military has admitted to attacking a tanker that killed three Indian seafarers. The incident occurred on June 10, when the US struck a Palau-flagged tanker, Settebello, resulting in the deaths of three out of 24 Indian sailors on board. The US military claimed the tanker violated its blockade. Additionally, another vessel, the Guinea-Bissau-flagged tanker Jalveer, with 20 Indian crew members, was attacked on Thursday, but all crew members were rescued. Oman's military has rescued dozens of Indian seafarers from the stricken ships. The Indian government has voiced a "strong protest" over the incident, which is the third US strike on vessels carrying Indian seafarers this week. The US used two Hellfire missiles in the attack on the Settebello tanker, according to reports. Bodies of the three killed Indian seafarers have been located and identified.

stories.headline: Allahabad High Court orders State to pay ₹2 lakh to man illegally detained for 8 days
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court ordered the Uttar Pradesh government to pay ₹2 lakh in compensation to a man who was illegally detained by police for eight days. The detention was in a breach of peace case, and the court criticized the UP Police for abusing preventive detention laws. The compensation is to be paid at a rate of ₹25,000 per day and must be paid within six weeks. The court also ordered that the amount be recovered from the salary of the erring Assistant Commissioner of Police. The man, a resident of Prayagraj, was held in illegal police custody, prompting the court to take serious note of the incident and direct the state government to pay compensation. The order was made in the case of Mansoor Ahmad @ Lallu and another v State of UP and 4 Others.

stories.headline: Saayoni Ghosh, Yusuf Pathan among 19 TMC rebel MPs
stories.summary: Nineteen Trinamool Congress (TMC) rebel MPs, including Saayoni Ghosh and Yusuf Pathan, have signed a letter to Speaker Om Birla's office. The list of signatories also includes Satabdi Roy, June Malia, Rachna Banerjee, and Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar. These MPs are part of a rebel group that may form a separate faction, pushing the TMC towards a vertical split. The development comes as the party faces a potential split, with 20 MPs allegedly joining the rebel camp backing the NDA. The submission of the letter to the Speaker's office is a significant move, indicating a deepening divide within the TMC. The rebel MPs' decision may have significant implications for the party's future and its leadership under Mamata Banerjee.

stories.headline: Can Speaker ignore TMC's choice for Leader of Opposition? Calcutta High Court to decide
stories.summary: The Calcutta High Court will decide if the Speaker of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly can ignore a party's choice for Leader of Opposition. The Trinamool Congress (TMC) has challenged Speaker Rathindra Bose's decision to appoint Ritabrata Banerjee, a rebel TMC MLA, as the Leader of the Opposition. The TMC had chosen a different leader, but the Speaker recognized Banerjee, who leads a breakaway faction of the party. The TMC moved the court seeking an urgent hearing, citing the first session of the 18th West Bengal Assembly scheduled to begin on June 18. The court will consider the matter, which involves the Speaker's authority to recognize a Leader of the Opposition contrary to the party's choice. The case, Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay v Hon'ble Speaker, West Bengal Legislative Assembly, will be heard by the court.

stories.headline: US Vs Iran At The World Cup? The July 3 Scenario That Could Turn Sport Into Geopolitics
stories.summary: Iran has announced it will not participate in the 2026 FIFA World Cup hosted in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The decision comes after Iran accused the US of "abusing its role as a World Cup host" by issuing heavily restricted visas to the Iranian team. Despite this, there was a possibility of the US and Iran facing each other in the tournament, with a mathematical probability of 17%. However, with Iran's withdrawal, this scenario is no longer possible. The situation is complicated by ongoing geopolitical tensions, including a war involving one of the tournament hosts and a participant. Iran's decision to withdraw from the World Cup highlights the challenges of separating sports from geopolitics in international competitions. The withdrawal has significant implications for the tournament and its participants.

stories.headline: Top US Expert Reveals The 3 Hidden Signs Of Real Burnout
stories.summary: A top US expert has identified three hidden signs of real burnout. Research shows that 65% of individuals with burnout experience frequent headaches, compared to 41% without burnout. Decreasing productivity and competence is another sign, leading to feelings of shame or guilt. The explosion of meetings and the resulting need to work after hours can contribute to burnout, making the workday feel infinite. Burnout detection tools, such as WorkTime, track signs of overwork by monitoring overtime patterns and after-hours activity, allowing managers to spot employees at risk early. Experts emphasize that burnout is not always easy to spot, and these hidden signs can be indicative of a larger issue. By recognizing these signs, individuals and managers can take steps to prevent and address burnout. Early warning signs can help mitigate the negative effects of burnout on employees and organizations.

stories.headline: No other headlines are provided to select from, only two are given.
stories.summary: A federal judge has blocked measures preventing officials from granting asylum, green cards, and other legal immigration benefits to many immigrants. The ruling, reported 3 hours ago by Eric P. Schmitt, affects immigration policies. In other news, the Arlington Fire Department responded to a hazmat incident at the Pentagon. Meanwhile, only one of the four House Republicans behind the Epstein files law will return to Congress next year. Various news outlets, including NBC News, BBC News, and CBS News, are providing coverage of these and other top stories, including breaking news, videos, and analysis on world news, business, politics, health, and pop culture. These outlets offer a range of perspectives and updates on current events, available on their websites and mobile apps.

stories.summary: Only one of the four House Republicans behind the Epstein files law will return to Congress next year. The law, which was recently passed, aims to make it easier for victims of Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking ring to access documents related to his case. The development comes as various news outlets continue to provide updates on the story, with NBC News, Hindustan Times, CNN, and MailOnline offering the latest coverage on the topic, as well as other breaking news stories in world events, politics, health, and entertainment. The news of the lawmakers' departure from Congress has been reported by Eric P. Schmitt, with further details and analysis available on the respective news websites.

stories.headline: 12 years of Modi govt: The new normal and what comes next
stories.summary: Narendra Modi has completed 12 years as Prime Minister of India, marking a significant milestone in the country's political landscape. During his tenure, Modi's government has implemented various initiatives aimed at improving governance and the lives of citizens. He highlighted that projects once taking decades to complete are now being finished in months, showcasing the government's efficiency. The government's commitment to "Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas" has been credited with strengthening governance and improving public services. Key decisions made during Modi's rule have reshaped India's political and policy landscape, with the opposition INDIA bloc still struggling to find a clear way to challenge him. As Modi's government looks to the future, it is expected to continue its focus on development and governance.

stories.headline: INDIA bloc struggles to find footing against Modi's BJP
stories.summary: INDIA bloc leaders met in New Delhi to reinforce unity and strategize against the ruling BJP. The meeting aimed to bridge internal differences and tackle economic challenges, with discussions focusing on protecting democratic principles. Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge raised concerns about India's economic, social, and foreign policy issues, as well as the electoral roll revision process. The bloc made five key decisions and planned its future strategy, despite the absence of DMK and AAP. The meeting is crucial for the alliance, which has suffered setbacks in recent assembly polls in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu. The INDIA bloc seeks to regroup and unify the opposition against the Narendra Modi government, addressing internal rifts and challenges to present a strong front. The meeting marks a renewed effort to confront national issues through collective decision-making.

stories.headline: Modi's 12-year report card: Hits and misses that defined his tenure
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 12-year tenure has been marked by significant reforms and achievements. He has spent over 9,000 days as the elected head of a government, including 12 years as Chief Minister of Gujarat and 12 years as Prime Minister. The Modi government has implemented key reforms such as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and demonetisation, altering India's economic landscape. However, the opposition has questioned the government's governance record, citing rising prices of essential commodities and high unemployment rates, with four out of ten graduates remaining unemployed. Despite this, Modi has highlighted major achievements in infrastructure development, calling his tenure a "collective yagya" and a form of public service. The government's record has been subject to scrutiny, with the Congress releasing a report card titled "Prachar vs Hisab" on the Modi government's 12th anniversary.

stories.headline: What the next phase of Modi's government could look like for India
stories.summary: Narendra Modi has become the longest-serving head of government in India since the 1952 elections, surpassing previous records. The Cabinet gave him a standing ovation to mark this milestone. Modi has been serving as the Prime Minister of India since 2014, previously holding the position of Chief Minister of Gujarat from 2001 to 2014. Elections are currently underway in Assam, Kerala, and Puducherry, seen as an early test of support for Modi's government. The latest schemes and achievements of the Modi government are available on the official website, along with live events and speech videos. With millions of Indians voting, the results of these elections will be closely watched as an indicator of the government's popularity and a potential glimpse into the next phase of Modi's administration. Modi's tenure has now exceeded 4,399 days.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Today: Sensex, Nifty Rally on US-Iran Peace Deal Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty surged significantly in early trade, tracking a global rally fueled by US President Donald Trump's declaration of an e
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty surged in early trade, driven by a global rally fueled by US President Donald Trump's declaration of a potential US-Iran peace deal. The Sensex rose nearly 1,000 points, while the Nifty crossed 12,350. Global markets, including Asia and Wall Street, rallied strongly after President Trump canceled planned Iran strikes, signaling a potential settlement. The easing of West Asia tensions and falling crude oil prices boosted investor sentiment, leading to a sharp rebound in Indian markets. The rally was a result of improved global market sentiment, with investors welcoming the de-escalation of tensions between the US and Iran. The drop in crude oil prices also contributed to the surge in Indian benchmark indices.

stories.headline: Stock market today: Sensex jumps 900 points, Nifty 50 above 23,400 - 5 key reasons behind Dalal Street rally
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant rally, with the Sensex jumping 900 points and the Nifty 50 surpassing 23,400. This surge was driven by a recovery in banking and IT stocks. The market had previously witnessed a sharp decline, with the Sensex plunging 1,456 points and the Nifty slipping below 23,400. However, hopes of a US-Iran peace deal and a record dividend payout of ₹2.11 lakh crore by the RBI contributed to the recent rally. The RBI's payout helped alleviate fiscal deficit concerns, boosting investor sentiment. The market's volatility has been influenced by global tensions and uncertainty surrounding the Middle East situation, but the current rally has lifted the Sensex to 76,617.44 and the Nifty above 23,400.

stories.headline: Sensex rises 1,000 pts intra-day; Nifty above 23,450: Key reasons here
stories.summary: The Sensex rose 1,695.40 points to 75,527.95, a 2.30% increase, while the Nifty index gained 461.30 points to 23,622.90, a 1.99% increase. During the day, the Sensex surged 1,000 points intra-day, with the Nifty crossing 23,450. The rally was driven by several factors, including easing geopolitical tensions and a fall in crude oil prices. Metal and banking stocks also contributed to the gains, with the indices turning rangebound after the initial surge. The increase marked a strong close to the fiscal year 2023, with the Sensex and Nifty indices ending on a high note. The market's positive performance was attributed to a combination of domestic and global factors, leading to a significant uptick in investor sentiment.

stories.headline: Why is market rising today? Sensex zooms 1,000 points, Nifty above 23,400. 4 key factors powering the rally
stories.summary: The Indian stock market has surged, with the Sensex rising over 1,000 points and the Nifty exceeding 23,400. Four key factors are driving this rally: optimism over a potential US-Iran peace deal, a decline in oil prices below $90, a global market rally, and an increase in the value of the rupee. The recovery in banking and IT stocks has also contributed to the market's growth. The Sensex closed at 76,617.44, up 592.93 points or 0.78%, while the Nifty index also saw significant gains. The cancellation of US strikes on Iran and hints at a peace deal have eased oil prices and inflation concerns, boosting global market sentiment and contributing to the rally in Indian markets.

stories.headline: Canadian mother sues OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT led to daughter's death
stories.summary: A Canadian mother has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, alleging that the company's chatbot, ChatGPT, contributed to her daughter's death. This lawsuit is one of several recent cases against OpenAI, including a California couple suing over the death of their teenage son, who allegedly used ChatGPT before taking his own life. Another lawsuit was filed by the heirs of a Connecticut woman, claiming that ChatGPT intensified mental health issues that led to a murder-suicide. The lawsuits raise concerns about the potential risks and consequences of using AI chatbots, particularly for vulnerable individuals. The cases, including Raine v. OpenAI, are ongoing, with the Canadian mother's lawsuit being the latest to be filed in a US court. The allegations highlight the need for further investigation into the impact of AI on mental health.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs Cuts 2027 Oil Price Estimate on Demand Uncertainty
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs has lowered its 2027 oil price forecast due to rising non-OPEC supply growth and weakening Chinese oil demand. The bank cut its average Brent crude price forecast for 2027 to $80, down from $85 previously. This revision is attributed to stronger supply growth and persistent weakness in demand, driven by electrification and alternative transport. Goldman Sachs expects Brent crude prices to average around $90 a barrel in the fourth quarter of 2026, before declining to around $66 by the fourth quarter of 2026. The bank's forecast for 2027 is $70 for Brent and $66 for WTI. Current prices are around $86.11 per barrel, with the bank having made two previous reductions to its forecast in the past six months. The revised forecast reflects the impact of weaker demand and pre-existing oversupply on oil prices.

stories.headline: Vietnam police bust group planning large-scale online scam centre
stories.summary: Vietnamese police have busted a transnational group planning to set up a large-scale online scam centre in Phu Tho province. The group, linked to online fraud syndicates in Cambodia, had rented premises and installed computer systems, mobile phones, and internet broadcasting equipment. They also set up office furniture, bunk beds, and other items to support large-scale operations. Investigators said the operation was in its final stages of establishing a scam centre targeting victims through online channels. Four suspects were arrested, including one Chinese national and three Vietnamese citizens. The disruption of the group is part of a wider regional crackdown on cyber fraud networks across Southeast Asia. The Ministry of Public Security announced the bust, highlighting the efforts of Vietnamese authorities to prevent the establishment of a major scam hub in the country.

stories.headline: EasyJet flight takes off from wrong point of Luton Airport runway
stories.summary: An EasyJet flight took off from the wrong point of Luton Airport's runway. The incident is under investigation, but details of the specific flight, including the date and destination, are not provided. This is not the first safety concern for EasyJet at Luton Airport, as a previous incident occurred last year where an EasyJet flight cleared the runway just 65ft above the ground during take-off. The Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) is involved in investigating such incidents to ensure aviation safety. EasyJet has experienced other issues at Luton Airport, including flight delays and cancellations due to bad weather conditions. The airline has notified passengers of potential disruptions via airport speakers. The investigation into the incorrect take-off point is ongoing, and further details are awaited. The safety of passengers and crew is a top priority for the airline and regulatory bodies.

stories.headline: OpenAI Uncovers China-Linked AI Operation
stories.summary: OpenAI has uncovered a China-linked AI operation that built a surveillance tool to gather real-time reports on anti-Chinese social media posts in Western countries. The operation, accidentally revealed by a Chinese law enforcement official's use of ChatGPT, aimed to intimidate Chinese dissidents abroad, including by impersonating US immigration officials. The campaign also targeted OpenAI with allegations of compromised user data and used ChatGPT to manipulate American public opinion on AI data centers and tariffs. Prompts connected to the operation instructed the AI model to criticize President Donald Trump while excluding Chinese President Xi Jinping. OpenAI disrupted the influence campaign, with principal investigator Ben Nimmo stating this is the first time the company has uncovered an AI-powered surveillance tool of this kind. The discovery highlights the growing use of AI in surveillance and influence operations.

stories.headline: OpenAI Acquires Ona to Strengthen Its Codex Programming Assistant
stories.summary: OpenAI has agreed to acquire Ona, a startup specializing in cloud execution environments for AI agents. The acquisition aims to enhance the capabilities of OpenAI's AI coding assistant, Codex, allowing it to handle longer-running and more sophisticated software development tasks. Ona's technology will enable Codex to take on more complex tasks, turning it into a full software-development platform. The deal is also expected to help enterprises deploy AI agents into production environments more effectively, strengthening enterprise security and expanding cloud execution capabilities. This acquisition is part of OpenAI's strategy to accelerate AI adoption and improve Codex's functionality, enabling persistent AI agents and more efficient software development processes. The move marks a significant step in OpenAI's efforts to enhance its coding assistant and expand its capabilities in the enterprise sector.

stories.headline: Satya Nadella says AI backlash is real but predicts higher wages and broader prosperity
stories.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella acknowledges a backlash against artificial intelligence in the US, but believes it will ultimately boost wages and lead to broader prosperity. He plans to invest $80 billion in Azure, Microsoft's cloud platform, to support AI development. Nadella warns of imminent AI-driven job displacement and urges companies and workers to adapt and reskill to remain relevant. He expresses optimism about India's ability to manage the transition to an AI-driven economy, citing the country's policy tools and technological capabilities. Nadella predicts that AI-led businesses could account for 10% of India's $5 trillion economy. He also shares a cautious view on artificial general intelligence, differing from some of his peers in the tech industry. Overall, Nadella emphasizes the need for stakeholders to work together to ensure a positive outcome from AI adoption.

stories.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX IPOs Could End Big Tech's Grip On AI Trade
stories.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX are preparing to go public, with SpaceX set to IPO this month and the other two having filed confidential preparations. SpaceX plans to sell 555 million shares at $135 each, which would be the largest IPO ever. OpenAI and Anthropic's valuations are expected to be significant, with the three companies commanding rare valuations in public markets. The IPOs come as investors seek explosive growth in AI, and the companies' listings will subject their AI businesses to quarterly scrutiny from Wall Street. The move may shift the structure of the AI trade, potentially ending Big Tech's grip on the industry. The companies' continued embedding of their bots across the economy has positioned them for significant growth and valuation. Experts warn of a potential "reality check" amidst the IPO race.
